RFC6793-3-1.note: TestRFC6793AS4PathWireExcludesConfed: AS4Path.WriteTo/Len skip both confed types and keep AS_SEQUENCE/AS_SET, with Len matching bytes written.

RFC6793-4.1-4.note: TestRFC6793EncodeFourOctetToNewSpeaker drives ASPath/Aggregator WriteToWithContext with an ASN4 context and asserts 4-byte AS_PATH stride and 8-octet AGGREGATOR; the negative shows the 2-octet form without the capability.

RFC6793-4.1-5.note: TestRFC6793DecodeFourOctetWhenNegotiated reads ParseASPath/ParseAggregator with fourByte=true and recovers 4200000001; the negative shows the same bytes decode on a 2-octet stride and an 8-octet AGGREGATOR is refused without the capability.

RFC6793-4.1-6.note: RFC 6793 §4.1 states: 'The new attributes, AS4_PATH and AS4_AGGREGATOR, MUST NOT be carried in an UPDATE message between NEW BGP speakers.' Section 6 repeats the prohibition. Re-read both primary passages, summary and unannotated checklist row, all five tagged covers and actual producers. TestOriginatedUpdateOmitsAS4PathTowardNewSpeaker drives the seven enumerated AS_PATH builder entry points with a non-mappable AS, asserting no decoded AS4_PATH AS numbers and the exact four-octet AS_PATH; TestOriginatedAggregatorOmitsAS4AggregatorTowardNewSpeaker drives all four enumerated aggregator builders, asserting attribute-18 absence and the real non-mappable AS in AGGREGATOR. The actual origination gates are UpdateBuilder.appendASPath/ASPathNeedsAS4 and appendAggregator/AS4AggregatorFor. The two NEW-speaker CI carriers supply the forbidden attributes rather than merely observing their absence on clean input: no-as4path requires exactly 24 attribute octets and preserves AS_PATH tail 4200000123 rather than the supplied AS4_PATH tail 4200000000; no-as4aggregator requires exactly 35 attribute octets, preserves AGGREGATOR AS 4200000123 and excludes the supplied AS4_AGGREGATOR naming 4200000000. Each exact full frame also requires delivery of the route. The OLD-speaker negative carrier requires the actual relayed two-octet AS_PATH [65000,65001,AS_TRANS] and four-octet AS4_PATH [65000,65001,4200000123], distinguishing the destination-scoped prohibition from blanket suppression; it is not an independent negative for AS4_AGGREGATOR. Current receive validation prepares AS4FamilyPlan, session_read consumes its WriteTo result before publication, and WriteTo explicitly omits types 17 and 18 while copying unrelated attributes and NLRI. The corrected comment names that actual path. Current WriteTo halt records in job-final-functional-citations-and-precise-framing-8381327b.log prove reachability only, since replay/EOR can fail before byte comparison; the older CollapseAS4Family-wrapper halt is not semantic evidence for these fixtures. The combined origination and exact relay assertions support both named attributes without treating either single carrier or a halt as proof of the whole clause.

RFC6793-4.1-7.note: RFC 6793 §4.1 states: 'A NEW BGP speaker that receives the AS4_PATH attribute or the AS4_AGGREGATOR attribute in an UPDATE message from another NEW BGP speaker MUST discard the path attribute and continue processing the UPDATE message.' Section 6 repeats that sentence; its following logging SHOULD is a separate obligation, not silently included in this verdict. Re-read the primary passages, summary and unannotated checklist row, all three tagged covers, ReconcileASPathFamily and the actual receive preparation/rewrite/publication consumers. TestRFC6793NewSpeakerAS4AttributesAreDiscarded feeds both attributes with SourceASN4=true, requires successful reconciliation, exact unchanged canonical AS_PATH and AGGREGATOR, and exactly the discard codes [AttrAS4Path,AttrAS4Aggregator]. Its AS_PATH and AS4_PATH values agree, so that value equality alone does not distinguish a mistaken merge; the explicit discard assertions and the live AS4_PATH carrier supply the missing distinction. That carrier deliberately disagrees on the path tail and requires the complete relayed frame containing the original AS_PATH, ORIGIN, NEXT_HOP and announced prefix, with no AS4_PATH: retaining it, substituting its tail, dropping the UPDATE or treating its route as withdrawn cannot satisfy the expectation. TestRFC6793ReceivedAS4PathAcceptedAlongsideASPath supplies the OLD-source control and requires the AS4_PATH's non-mappable AS to become canonical instead of retaining AS_TRANS. The unit cover establishes both attribute decisions; the CI tagged to this ID establishes continued route processing and non-substitution end to end for AS4_PATH only, not an AS4_AGGREGATOR-specific end-to-end claim. Source inspection confirms the shared AS4FamilyPlan.WriteTo dispatch explicitly drops both legacy attributes, preserves unrelated attributes and NLRI, and returns the rewritten WireUpdate for normal callback publication. The separately tagged AS4_AGGREGATOR carrier under RFC6793-4.1-6 corroborates that same writer boundary but is not misrepresented as a tagged cover of this ID. Whole-producer halts remain reachability evidence, not selective discard proof. The combined tagged unit and functional assertions enforce both discard and continued-processing obligations.

RFC6793-4.2.1-1.note: TestRFC6793OpenMyASIsASTransWithoutTwoOctetAS asserts the sent OPEN My AS is 23456 for AS 4200000001; the negative keeps 65001 as itself.

RFC6793-4.2.2-1.note: TestRFC6793EncodeTwoOctetToOldSpeaker asserts a 2-octet AS_PATH with AS_TRANS toward a non-ASN4 context; the negative keeps mappable ASNs unsubstituted.

RFC6793-4.2.2-2.note: Originate builders (message) and TranscodeASPath (wireu) both emit AS4_PATH with the real 4-octet AS toward an OLD speaker; negatives show no AS4_PATH when every AS is mappable.

RFC6793-4.2.2-3.note: Originate builders and TranscodeASPath omit AS4_PATH when all ASNs are mappable; negatives show it present for a non-mappable AS.

RFC6793-4.2.2-4.note: Both confederation types now proven excluded from the constructed AS4_PATH. TestRFC6793ConstructedAS4PathExcludesConfedSet: AS_CONFED_SET {64514,64515}, AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE [64512], AS_SEQUENCE [non-mappable, 65001] through TranscodeASPath 4->2 yields an AS4_PATH of exactly the one AS_SEQUENCE, AS_PATH keeping all three. The AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE half is also held by the HEAD TestRFC6793ConstructedAS4PathExcludesConfed (exact single-segment assertion, no record) and by the AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE inside the new recorded unit. Negative TestRFC6793ConstructedAS4PathKeepsAnOrdinarySet: an ordinary AS_SET in the same place is carried, so the exclusion is scoped to type 3/4. Judge break (overlay, attribute/as4.go AS4Path.Len and WriteTo excluding only AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE) turned the new positive red, the HEAD sequence-only unit and the new negative green. Revert records on TranscodeASPath both polarities.

RFC6793-4.2.2-5.note: Three producers (message originate, wireu TranscodeASPath, rib commit pack) each send AS_TRANS in a 6-octet AGGREGATOR plus AS4_AGGREGATOR with the real AS for a non-mappable aggregator; negatives keep a mappable AS with no companion.

RFC6793-4.2.2-6.note: Same three producers send no AS4_AGGREGATOR for a mappable aggregating AS; negatives show it present for a non-mappable one.

RFC6793-4.2.3-1.note: TestRFC6793ReceivedAS4PathAcceptedAlongsideASPath: ReconcileASPathFamily accepts AS_PATH+AS4_PATH from an OLD speaker and uses the AS4_PATH ASNs; the negative shows no 4-octet AS invented without AS4_PATH.

RFC6793-4.2.3-10.note: Judge 2026-09-30. TestRFC6793ConfedSegmentAdjacentToPrependedIsPrepended drives ReconcileASPathFamily: + AS_SEQ 64500, AS_CONFED_SEQ 65001, AS_SEQ TRANS TRANS beside a two-hop AS4_PATH keeps the confed segment after the prepended 64500; - the same confed segment behind a non-prepended AS_SEQ is dropped. Leading-segment clause is TestRFC6793LeadingConfedSegmentIsPrepended. Judge breaks in appendLeadingSegments: continuing past a non-prepended segment turned the negative red; stopping before a confed segment once the budget is spent turned the positive red.

RFC6793-4.2.3-2.note: TestRFC6793ReceivedAS4AggregatorAccepted: the AGGREGATOR+AS4_AGGREGATOR pair from an OLD speaker is accepted and the 4-octet aggregating AS survives ingest (single-polarity marker).

RFC6793-4.2.3-3.note: TestRFC6793AggregatorWithRealASIgnoresAS4Attributes: with AGGREGATOR.AS 64500 the AS4_PATH does not reach the path and the AS4_AGGREGATOR is discarded; negatives with AS_TRANS use both.

RFC6793-4.2.3-4.note: Same unit: the AGGREGATOR (64500, 10.0.0.1) is the aggregating node; the AS_TRANS counterpart does not take it.

RFC6793-4.2.3-5.note: Same unit: the route path is the AS_PATH widened with AS_TRANS intact; the AS_TRANS counterpart reconstructs instead.

RFC6793-4.2.3-6.note: TestRFC6793AggregatorWithASTransPromotesAS4Aggregator: with AGGREGATOR.AS AS_TRANS the stored aggregator is the AS4_AGGREGATOR value, not AS_TRANS; negative keeps a real-AS AGGREGATOR.

RFC6793-4.2.3-7.note: Same unit: the aggregating node is 4200000001/10.0.0.1 from AS4_AGGREGATOR; negatives: not promoted when AGGREGATOR is real, nor when AS4_AGGREGATOR arrives alone.

RFC6793-4.2.3-8.note: TestRFC6793LongerAS4PathIsIgnored: AS_PATH 2 ASNs vs AS4_PATH 3 yields the widened AS_PATH only; negative shows AS4_PATH used when AS_PATH is longer.

RFC6793-4.2.3-9.note: TestRFC6793LongerASPathPrependsLeadingHops, EqualCountsPrependNothing, LeadingASSetIsTakenWhole assert exact reconstructed bytes; negative: no prepend when AS4_PATH is longer.

RFC6793-6-1.note: TestRFC6793AS4PathMalformedRejected drives every Section 6 condition (odd length, <6 octets, zero and overrunning segment length, undefined type) through ParseAS4Path; positive accepts a well-formed path. The tag at rfc6793_reconcile_test.go TestRFC6793MalformedAS4PathIsDiscarded describes the RFC6793-6-4 discard obligation rather than this row.

RFC6793-6-2.note: TestRFC6793AS4AggregatorLengthEight: ParseAS4Aggregator accepts 8 octets and refuses 0,6,7,9,12 with ErrInvalidLength.

RFC6793-6-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-02 (BGP c34 judge). internal/component/bgp/wireu/rfc6793_received_confed_test.go reads the output of CollapseAS4Family, the single ingest rewrite every downstream consumer sees, so the receive-side discard is measured apart from the AS4_PATH encoder's own confed filter (RFC6793-3-1). Positive: an OLD speaker's AS4_PATH holding an AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE and an AS_CONFED_SET ahead of an AS_SEQUENCE collapses to the exact payload (AS_PATH 40 02 10: [65001] then [4200000001,4200000002], attribute section 0x1E, NLRI kept, no error): both segment types discarded, lengths adjusted, processing continues (judge checked the RFC 6793 Section 4.2.3 arithmetic and both length octets). Negative: an AS_SET in the AS4_PATH and a leading AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE in the AS_PATH both survive (payload literal, 0x1C / 0x2A), so the discard is not blanket. Records: attribute/as4.go::appendAS4Segments revert, both polarities observed red; author overlay probes (kept confed segments -> only the positive red, discard widened to AS_SET -> only the negative red) re-read by the judge in scratch c34p. The HEAD egress units in rfc6793_as4_test.go stay as unrecorded supplementary tags. The Section 6 SHOULD-log clause is not this row.

RFC6793-6-4.note: TestRFC6793MalformedAS4PathDiscarded: an odd-length AS4_PATH from an OLD speaker contributes nothing and the rewrite proceeds; negative keeps a well-formed one.

RFC6793-6-5.note: TestCollapseAS4DiscardsMalformedAS4Aggregator: a 7-octet AS4_AGGREGATOR is removed from the collapsed payload, not promoted, NLRI kept, drop reported; negative reads an 8-octet one.
